page: Amazon Web Services d2.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance under the D2 generation, engineered for applications requiring massive local disk space. It runs on the Xen hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2676 v3 processor clocked at 2.4 GHz. The instance delivers 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled (2 threads per core), supported by a 30 MB L3 cache, 122.0 GB of memory (7.62 GB per physical core), and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. It includes no dedicated GPUs.

The defining characteristic of the d2.4xlarge is its bundled local storage, offering 24,576 GB of local hard disk drive (HDD) capacity. Compute benchmarks reveal modest execution rates typical of older Haswell-generation architectures. Single-core tests such as Geekbench single-core (895.0) and stress-ng single-core (742.99) fall within the bottom 10%, while multi-core workloads yield average scores, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 5383.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 14,324.65. Uncached large-block memory writes measure 19.85 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the lower 25%.

Given its substantial 24 TB local HDD footprint, the d2.4xlarge trades single-threaded compute and fast random disk access for high-density sequential storage capacity. It is primarily suited for sequential read/write big data processing, data warehousing, Hadoop distributed file systems (HDFS), log collection, and batch ETL pipelines where total disk density outweighs raw compute velocity.
